item.title: Bridging digitalisation, sustainability, and resilience through systems thinking tools: Integrated perspectives and collaborative practices for SMEs
item.content:encoded:
Rui Torres de Oliveira, Deakin University

Agnes Toth-Peter, University of Queensland

Martie-Louise Verreynne, University of Queensland

David Audretsch, Indiana University

Domenico Dentoni, MBS School of Business

Andrea Chiarini, University of Verona

The 21st century presents a range of complex and interdependent challenges, including climate change, resource depletion, economic inequality, and technological disruptions. These so-called wicked problems demand a paradigm shift in our approach to problem-solving. Addressing such challenges requires multi-stakeholder partnerships and holistic, systems-level approaches that transcend traditional, siloed methodologies. Systems thinking, a powerful tool for understanding complexity and interconnections, offers a pathway to sustainable solutions.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of systems thinking tools, such as causal loop diagrams (CLDs), system archetypes, and system dynamics modeling, in addressing sustainability challenges
  • Development and validation of systems-level frameworks and methodologies for sustainable development
  • Case studies demonstrating the impact of systems thinking on real-world sustainability and/or digitalisation initiatives
  • Use of group model building and participatory system dynamics to support interdisciplinary and ecosystem solutions
  • Exploration of system archetypes and system dynamics models to identify leverage points for driving transformational change and to investigate levers in cross-boundary settings
  • The role of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, big data, and blockchain, in enabling systems-level insights and solutions in the circular economy and sustainability initiatives
  • Integration of digitalisation with circular economy strategies and Industry 5.0 principles and potentials
  • Innovative approaches to digital transformation that promote sustainable development
  • Cross-sectoral and interdisciplinary research to foster collaboration in bridging sustainability and digitalisation, using systems thinking
  • The role of ecosystems in sustainable business models and the boundaries of entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Methodologies for recognising, assessing and addressing the interconnectedness of environmental, economic, and social systems
  • Open innovation in new sustainable businesses, considering distinct institutional contexts and economic systems, such as emerging and developed economies

Timeline

  • October 1, 2026: Rolling submissions begin
  • May 31, 2027: Manuscript deadline for rolling submissions

item.title: Digitalization for responsive and circular supply chains
item.content:encoded:
Günter Prockl, Copenhagen Business School

Alexander Pflaum, University of Bamberg

Haozhe Chen, Iowa State University

Marcel Papert, University of Bamberg

Modern supply chains face unprecedented disruptions while simultaneously confronting environmental limits and resource scarcity. This requires a fundamental transformation toward more responsive and circular systems. Digital technologies including IoT, AI, digital twins, and blockchain are critical enablers for building resilient supply chains that adapt quickly to change while reducing resource consumption and closing material loops.

The special issue seeks papers demonstrating how digital and data-driven solutions implement these responsive and circular supply chains, along with their associated business models. Contributions should explore digital technologies across multiple supply chain tiers, with particular emphasis on industry-specific applications and the integration of responsiveness, servitization, and sustainability goals.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Contribution of digital technologies to responsiveness, agility, flexibility, adaptability, improvisation, and resilience, sustainability, circularity, and regeneration
  • Increasing supply chain visibility based on digital technologies
  • AI methods supporting forecasting, planning, decision making and optimization
  • Division of labour and interactions between humans and machines in AI-supported supply chains
  • Virtualization and simulation of supply chains based on digital twins
  • Blockchain and smart contracts in logistics and supply chain management
  • The role of digital platforms in supply chain management
  • Effects of smart product-service-systems on supply chains and supply chain management
  • Ecosystems and federated data ecosystems enabling new data-driven R strategies
  • Models, methods and tools enabling the triple transformation of supply chains
  • Barriers and challenges hindering digitalization, servitization and transition to sustainability and circularity
  • Data security and cyber security challenges in digital supply chain structures
  • Legal aspects within the digital, servitized, circular supply chain
  • Potential of digital technologies for ensuring compliance with legal requirements in the context of sustainability and circularity
  • Relationship management mechanisms and governance structures in the era of digitalized supply chains

Timeline

  • October 15, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Digitalisation of and by projects: A sociotechnical perspective on the consequences for project work

item.title: The Interplay of Human Resource Management and Leadership: Alignment, Tensions, and Consequences
item.content:encoded:
Aneeqa Suhail, Tilburg University

Steven Kilroy, Trinity College Dublin

Robin Bauwens, Tilburg University

Sut I Wong, BI Norwegian Business School

Sasa Batistič, Tilburg University

Managing people in organizations requires a combination of Human Resource Management (HRM) and leadership, often referred to as 'people management'. While HRM provides formalized systems, practices, and architectures that structure employment relationships, leadership shapes how these systems are enacted, interpreted, and given meaning in everyday work. Therefore, the outcomes traditionally associated with people management do not emerge from HRM or leadership in isolation, but from their ongoing interrelationship across organizational levels.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Human Resource Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How HRM systems and leadership behaviors interact in shaping employee and organizational outcomes across organizational levels
  • How different forms of alignment between HRM and leadership (e.g., supplementary fit, complementary fit, perceptual filtering) produce distinct employee and organizational outcomes
  • When and how HRM systems function as substitutes for leadership, and what are the resulting consequences for employee and organizational outcomes
  • How misalignment between HRM systems and leadership behaviors emerge, persist, or become institutionalized within organizations
  • When alignment between HRM systems and leadership amplifies negative outcomes such as work intensification, role overload, or employee strain
  • How employees interpret and respond to situations in which HRM systems substitute for, constrain, or contradict leadership behaviors
  • Which configurations of HRM systems and leadership forms strengthen the effectiveness and sustainability of remote and hybrid work arrangements
  • How leaders enact, adapt, or resist HRM systems when leading employees at a distance, and how does this shape employees' sensemaking and experiences of people management
  • How employees experience alignment, misalignment, or substitution between HRM systems and leadership in remote and hybrid work settings, and how do these experiences affect employee and organizational outcomes
  • How HRM–leadership configurations evolve over time and how do these experiences affect pertinent employee and organizational outcomes
  • How alignment, misalignment, and substitution between HRM and leadership shape employee well-being and performance over time
  • How temporal shifts in leadership behaviors or HRM systems alter the balance between substitution and complementarity

  • March 31, 2027: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: Reflections on the value of management accounting in organizations: Overcoming contemporary challenges
item.content:encoded:
Teemu Laine, Tampere University

Tuomas Korhonen, Tampere University

Carsten Rohde, Copenhagen Business School

Vesa Tiitola, Tampere University

The special issue will reflect and revisit the role and value of management accounting (MA) in the current evolving and complex business context. The value of management accounting lies in its ability to serve managers in different roles in their decision making and broader managerial work, all situated in their operational environment. The nature of managerial work and the potential support from MA therein are being challenged by several intertwined contemporary developments: a) technology advancements, such as algorithms and the artificial intelligence (AI) penetration to many professions, MA included, b) human judgement, ethical considerations and responsible behaviour, and c) global and local issues that influence the business context, such as geopolitics and climate change.

Appel publié par Qualitative Research in Accounting & Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Revisiting the Foundations of Management Accounting (MA) and Management Control (MC)
  • Digitalization, Artificial Intelligence, and the "Post-Analytics" Era
  • Human Judgment and Accountability in the Age of AI
  • Sustainability, Ethics, and the Evolving Role of Management Accounting
  • Transformation and Innovation in MA&MC Systems and Practices
  • Management Accounting that Expands over Organizational Boundaries
  • Emerging Business Models and Performance Paradigms
  • Inter-, Multi-, and Transdisciplinary MA Studies that Increase Practical Relevance of Research

Timeline

  • June 8, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • September 30, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission
